questions.question: How should it get power?
questions.why: Every board needs a supply; the right one decides the connector, the regulator and the size.

options.label: USB-C
options.detail: 5 V from any phone charger or laptop

options.label: A coin cell
options.detail: Tiny; good for a blinker or a sensor that sleeps
options.add: powered by a CR2032 coin cell

options.label: A rechargeable LiPo
options.add: powered by a LiPo battery with USB charging

questions.question: How big can it be?
questions.why: A tighter board costs less and fits more places, a roomier one is easier to solder and label.

options.label: As small as possible
options.detail: Parts packed tight, both sides if it helps
options.add: keep the board as small as possible

options.label: Comfortable
options.add: leave room between parts for labels

questions.question: Anything on the board to help you debug it?
questions.why: A status LED and test points cost nothing on a prototype and save an evening.

options.label: A status LED
options.detail: One LED on a free pin

options.label: Test points
options.add: with test points on the main nets
